In the same study, xQuAD was reported as the only approach that consistently improved all three baseline rankers."}],"weight":1}],"rejected_claims":[{"text":"MMR's original SIGIR 1998 paper provides strong, large-sample user-study evidence that it improves web-search user satisfaction.","reason":"Unsupported by the supplied evidence; the evidence says the pilot had 5 users and was too small for statistically significant speed or recall trends."},{"text":"There is one universally best λ value for MMR.","reason":"Unsupported and overly broad; the supplied evidence says λ is user-tunable, gives endpoint interpretations, and mentions tuning or task-dependent use rather than a universal optimum."},{"text":"MMR uniformly improves diversified search results over pure relevance ranking.","reason":"Contradicted by the supplied evidence; Santos, Macdonald, and Ounis report cases where MMR hurt baseline rankings."},{"text":"xQuAD is always better than MMR in every search setting.","reason":"Overly broad; the supplied evidence only says xQuAD consistently improved all three baseline rankers in the cited WWW 2010 study."},{"text":"The strongest original evidence for MMR comes from multi-document summarization results at SUMMAC.","reason":"Not supported by the codex teacher-run evidence set used here; that detail appears only in the other run and is outside the selected evidence for these claims."}]}
